When `phrase_boundaries_ms` is present, this can move `raw_trim` later by up to several bars after `BarPlanner` has already clamped `per_body_bars` using the unsnapped grid trim. comment_body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Key grid windows by segment instead of track id**

If a set repeats the same `track_id` in two positions, this assignment overwrites the earlier solo window. `measure_body_bpm()` then looks up `bodies[tid]` for each segment, so every repeated occurrence is measured over the last occurrence's body and drift in the earlier occurrence can be missed or misreported. Store windows in segment order, or include the segment index, rather than keying only by `track_id`.

@@ -0,0 +1,113 @@
+"""Grid-alignment check for a rendered mix (post-render QA).
+
+Phase measurement on a demucs-stem mix is unreliable (stems shift transients
+30-100ms — see AGENTS.md render lessons). The robust end-to-end signal is the
+**body BPM**: if rubberband honored ``tempo_ratio = bpm_measured / target``,
+every track body plays at exactly ``target_bpm``. BPM via envelope
+autocorrelation is phase-insensitive, so it survives the demucs/DSP chain.
+
+Checked on real renders: a wrong stored BPM produced +1.6 BPM drift on one
+track (max |dev| 1.60, mean 0.34); after the ``bpm_measured`` fix every track
+sat within 0.4 BPM (max 0.40, mean 0.09).
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+import numpy as np
+
+# Status thresholds (BPM) — from AGENTS.md lesson #4: a 0.5 BPM discrepancy is
+# audible on a 60s transition (~0.5 beat drift); >1.0 BPM is a real engine bug.
+OK_THRESHOLD_BPM = 0.5
+WARN_THRESHOLD_BPM = 1.0
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+class BodyBpm:
+    """One track's measured body BPM in the rendered mix."""
+
+    track_id: int
+    body_s: float
+    body_e: float
+    bpm_measured: float
+    bpm_dev: float
+
+    @property
+    def status(self) -> str:
+        return classify_dev(self.bpm_dev)
+
+
+def classify_dev(
+    dev_bpm: float, ok: float = OK_THRESHOLD_BPM, warn: float = WARN_THRESHOLD_BPM
+) -> str:
+    """Map an absolute BPM deviation to ok / warn / fail."""
+    a = abs(dev_bpm)
+    if a <= ok:
+        return "ok"
+    if a <= warn:
+        return "warn"
+    return "fail"
+
+
+def body_windows(segs: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]) -> dict[int, tuple[float, float]]:
+    """Per-track solo windows: [start+d_in, end-d_out], clipped at mix edges."""
+    out: dict[int, tuple[float, float]] = {}
+    n = len(segs)
+    for i, seg in enumerate(segs):
+        d_in = 0.0 if i == 0 else seg

comment_body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Report unmeasured body windows instead of OK**

When a body window is shorter than 20 beats, this path emits `bpm_measured=0` and `bpm_dev=0`; because `BodyBpm.status` is derived from the deviation, the handler counts the track as OK and can report `grid OK` without measuring that segment. This affects clamped/short tracks or bad plan windows and hides the cases that need QA, so return a warn/fail/unknown status instead of a zero-deviation OK row.

comment_body: `tempo` равен `target_bpm / source_bpm`; при `tempo > 1` rubberband ускоряет аудио и сокращает его длительность. Чтобы получить `event.duration_s` после rubberband, входной trim должен быть примерно `duration_s * tempo` (плюс запас), а не `duration_s / tempo`. На длинных событиях при ускорении текущая формула недодаёт исходный материал, и последующий `atrim=duration=...` не может восстановить потерянный хвост — возможны укороченные слои и gaps. Исправьте формулу и добавьте regression case для speed-up.

comment_body:
В текущем виде не могу рекомендовать merge: в рендерном пути есть три блокирующие проблемы.

1. Треки, не прошедшие feature scan, остаются кандидатами планировщика и могут дойти до ffmpeg.
2. Для ускорения tempo correction предварительный trim использует обратный коэффициент и обрезает длинные события.

comment_body:
## Blocking findings

1. **Subgenre presets mutate process-global settings.** In [`render_orchestrator.py:39-40`](https://github.com/evgenygurin/dj-music-plugin/blob/6a89fb298aec3c48edaa65ee8279544d9dce7f7f/app/handlers/_orchestrator/render_orchestrator.py#L39-L40), the cached `get_settings()` result is passed to `SubgenrePresetApplier`, whose `apply()` mutates it in [`subgenre_presets.py:51-56`](https://github.com/evgenygurin/dj-music-plugin/blob/6a89fb298aec3c48edaa65ee8279544d9dce7f7f/app/domain/performance/subgenre_presets.py#L51-L56). Because `get_settings()` is process-wide cached, one render with `subgenre` changes every later render and can race with concurrent renders. Make the settings object render-local (copy/clone before applying overrides) or make preset application pure.

2. **The requested subgenre bar preset is not used by the actual timeline.** `RenderOrchestrator` computes the `BarPlan` without passing `request.subgenre` ([`render_orchestrator.py:44-49`](https://github.com/evgenygurin/dj-music-plugin/blob/6a89fb298aec3c48edaa65ee8279544d9dce7f7f/app/handlers/_orchestrator/render_orchestrator.py#L44-L49)). `TrackInput` has no mood field, so `BarPlanner` falls back to the mixed-pair defaults in [`bar_plan.py:65-85`](https://github.com/evgenygurin/dj-music-plugin/blob/6a89fb298aec3c48edaa65ee8279544d9dce7f7f/app/domain/render/bar_plan.py#L65-L85); `RenderPlanner` then gives those per-track values precedence over the global settings at [`plan_assembler.py:54-65`](https://github.com/evgenygurin/dj-music-plugin/blob/6a89fb298aec3c48edaa65ee8279544d9dce7f7f/app/domain/render/plan_assembler.py#L54-L65). For example, the `dub_techno` preset's 64-bar transition/32-bar body values are applied to settings but the timeline still receives the mixed defaults (32/64). Pass the set-level preset into bar planning or otherwise make the preset values authoritative unless explicit request overrides are supplied.

3. **Mixed prepared 4-stem and 5-stem libraries can crash instead of falling back.** `StemResolver` accepts either a complete Demucs 4-stem set or a complete prepared 5-stem set independently for each track ([`stem_resolver.py:38-44`](https://github.com/evgenygurin/dj-music-plugin/blob/6a89fb298aec3c48edaa65ee8279544d9dce7f7f/app/handlers/_orchestrator/stem_resolver.py#L38-L44)). If the set contains one of each, `_resolve_stem_order()` falls through to the 5-stem order in [`plan_assembler.py:24-31`](https://github.com/evgenygurin/dj-music-plugin/blob/6a89fb298aec3c48edaa65ee8279544d9dce7f7f/app/domain/render/plan_assembler.py#L24-L31), and `StemMultiDeckStrategy` indexes missing 5-stem keys on the 4-stem track ([`filtergraph.py:420-425`](https://github.com/evgenygurin/dj-music-plugin/blob/6a89fb298aec3c48edaa65ee8279544d9dce7f7f/app/domain/render/filtergraph.py#L420-L425)). Reject mixed layouts and use classic/Demucs fallback, or normalize all tracks to one stem order before building the plan.

4. **Prepared-stem rows are trusted without checking that their files still exist.** The DB path is accepted directly in [`stem_resolver.py:103-111`](https://github.com/evgenygurin/dj-music-plugin/blob/6a89fb298aec3c48edaa65ee8279544d9dce7f7f/app/handlers/_orchestrator/stem_resolver.py#L103-L111); only missing stem *names* trigger Demucs fallback at lines 113-124. A deleted or moved prepared file therefore looks like a complete stem set and reaches ffmpeg, producing a render failure instead of the advertised fallback. Validate each prepared path before returning it and treat stale paths as missing.

Please address these before merging; they affect render isolation, advertised subgenre semantics, and the 4/5-stem fallback guarantees.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Convert LUFS to power before summing layers**

For multi-stem `energy_budget` calls with two or more measured layers, this treats LUFS (a logarithmic dB quantity) as a linear amplitude. For example, two -10 LUFS stems are reported near -20 LUFS with +12 dB headroom to a -8 LUFS target, although their combined loudness is about -7 LUFS and should be flagged for attenuation; this inverts the headroom/recommendation signal for the layering decisions the tool is meant to guide.

1. `render_mixdown` now always builds `per_transition_bars`/`per_body_bars`, but both are derived from `getattr(inputs[i], "mood", None)`. `TrackInput` doesn’t define `mood` and `get_render_inputs()` doesn’t populate it, so every lookup is `None`, every pair resolves to `MIXED_PAIR`, and `build_render_plan` always applies those per-* lists. `sequence_optimize` can intentionally return a *subset* when some `track_ids` have no scoring features (the tool drops missing ids instead of failing when at least 2 valid ids remain). On scheduled or manual runs, this treats any open issue whose body contains the marker as a trusted Claude lane incident. Because this is a public repository, an external user can create such an issue and cause the secret-bearing paid probe to run; a healthy result will also let `resolveLaneReadinessAlerts` close that user-created issue. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Wait for cancellation before reconciling the run**

When GitHub has accepted the asynchronous cancellation request but still reports the run as `in_progress`, this immediately queued reconcile can execute too early. `reconcileActive` only terminalizes the ledger when `getWorkflowRun` returns `status === 'completed'` (`apps/dispatch-broker/src/main.ts:491`), so an early pass is a no-op and the cancelled generation remains active until the scheduled sweep. Poll for terminal status before notifying, or arrange another reconcile after cancellation completes.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve rerun access beyond the token's one-hour lifetime**

The new value is a GitHub App installation token, which expires after one hour, while the OpenCode adapter is explicitly allowed to run for 120 minutes. If the agent needs to rerun failed CI after the first hour, the documented `GH_TOKEN=$ACTIONS_RERUN_TOKEN gh run rerun ...` command now receives a 401; the previous `github.token` remained valid for the whole job. Use a narrow credential that remains refreshable or valid throughout the adapter's execution window.

comment_body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Check inherited environments and aliases in the boundary test**

This only scans the adapter step's literal source for one expression spelling. If the same credential is set in workflow/job-level `env`, the adapter inherits it but this assertion passes; `${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` and bracket-form context access can likewise expose the same job token without matching the regex. Since this test is intended to enforce the controller boundary against future workflow drift, it should account for inherited environments and equivalent references rather than only `${{ github.token }}` written directly inside the step.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

pr_title: feat(dispatch): Phase 3 — credential boundary + worker harness (#645)
comment_body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject real warnings even when zero sessions is also reported**

When every discovered transcript fails to read or reduce, `finalizeSidecar` emits those failure warnings and then also emits the permitted “finalize discovered zero sessions” warning because `shippedCount` remains zero. This condition therefore passes the canary whenever the benign substring appears anywhere in the log, masking exactly the transcript failures the preceding comment says are fatal. Filter out the permitted warning and fail if any other watcher warning remains.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

+The condition for safe decoupling — ensuring the cross-term does not introduce additional gain or phase crossings near either loop's crossover frequency:
 
 ```math
 \frac{f_i}{f_{i+1}} \geq 10 \quad \text{for all adjacent loop pairs} \qquad \text{(Eq. 5.6)}
 ```

The citations to `subSys.c (line 178)` are ambiguous in this repo because the checked-in source is `subSys.c,v` (RCS) and line numbers won’t match directly (and will drift over time). Prefer citing the function name (`subSysPhaseTot`) and the repository path (`spear-rf-code-legacy/rfApp/src/db/subSys.c,v`) without hard-coded line numbers, or clarify which line-number basis is being used.
```suggestion
The direct loop phase is computed by `subSysPhaseTot` in `spear-rf-code-legacy/rfApp/src/db/subSys.c,v`, which implements rate-limited delta tracking with frequency-offset compensation from the tuner position polynomial model. It computes the delta phase from frequency offset: `K = -0.000360 * group_delay * freq_offset * conv_const` (when loop and tracking are on), then tracks total phase as `L = L + rate_limited(C + D + K - L)` with +/-180 deg wrap.

> **Sources**: [R15]; [R14]; `subSysPhaseTot` in `spear-rf-code-legacy/rfApp/src/db/subSys.c,v` (phase computation); RFP module hardware.
```

 ## 6. Loop-by-Loop Transfer Functions and Design
 
-### 6.1 Direct Loop Specifications
+This section documents each feedback loop in the SPEAR3 LLRF system, ordered from fastest to slowest. All five active loops and the inactive PEP-II heritage features are covered with code-verified parameters.
+
+### 6.0 Loop Bandwidth Hierarchy
+
+The following table summarizes the complete bandwidth hierarchy. Adjacent loops are separated by at minimum the required factor of 10 in bandwidth (Eq. 5.6), ensuring frequency-domain decoupling.
+
+| Loop | Bandwidth | Disturbance | Implementation | Source File(s) |
+|------|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
+| Direct (feedback) | ~800 kHz | D1–D4 | Analog (RFP module) | Hardware |
+| Ripple (harmonic) | 60–1500 Hz | D5 | DSP assembly (AT&T DSP1610) | `sp3ripple.s` |
+| HVPS (voltage) | ~0.1 Hz | D6 | EPICS SNL | `rf_hvps_loop.st` |
+| DAC (amplitude) | ~0.1 Hz | D6 | EPICS SNL | `rf_dac_loop.st` |
+| Tuner (frequency) | ~0.01 Hz | D7, D8 | EPICS SNL | `rf_tuner_loop.st` |
+
+**Separation ratios** (code-verified from maximum cycle times):
+
+| Adjacent Pair | Ratio | Requirement |
+|:-:|:-:|:-:|
+| Direct / Ripple | ~500x | >= 10x |
+| Ripple / HVPS | ~600x | >= 10x |
+| Ripple / DAC | ~600x | >= 10x |
+| HVPS and DAC | ~1x | Co-equal, orthogonal actuators |
+| DAC / Tuner | ~10x | >= 10x |

 ### 4.6 D6: Klystron Gain Variation
 
-Small-signal gain varies up to $\sim 7$ dB over the operating range. The gain tracking function (§6.9) compensates by adjusting I/Q modulator weights.
+**Source of gain variation**: As beam current changes from 0 to 500 mA, the HVPS loop adjusts cathode voltage $V_k$ to maintain the klystron $\sim 10\%$ below saturation. As $V_k$ changes, the small-signal gain (slope of the $P_\text{out}$ vs $P_\text{in}$ curve) varies by up to $\sim 7$ dB. This shifts the open-loop gain of the direct feedback loop, potentially affecting stability margins.
+
+**Gain tracking implementation** (§6.9): The baseband modulator on the RFP module (4 Gilbert-cell multipliers in a 2×2 matrix) has its matrix coefficients controlled by 12-bit Octal DACs. A slow EPICS loop ($\sim 2$ Hz) reads the klystron forward power and drive power monitors, computes the current gain, and adjusts the modulator matrix to maintain constant overall loop gain:
+
+```math
+G_\text{modulator} = \frac{G_\text{loop,target}}{G_\text{klystron}(V_k)} \qquad \text{(Eq. 4.6a)}
+```
+
+The MATLAB calibration routine `ConfDirect` (initiated from the EPICS feedback panel) performs the initial gain tracking setup by measuring klystron gain at the current operating point and writing the appropriate 2×2 matrix coefficients to the quad DAC.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject non-test-failure pytest exit codes**

When pytest exits after an interruption or internal/usage error but the CTRF plugin has still written a readable report, this path scores the report and eventually clears `verifier_error.txt`, so `scripts/check_run_results.py` classifies an incomplete or broken verifier run as a genuine FAIL and may even retain partial credit. Pytest reserves exit code 1 for failed tests; codes 2–5 represent interruption, internal error, usage error, or no tests collected ([pytest exit-code reference](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/reference/exit-codes.html)). Only status 1 should enter partial scoring; other nonzero statuses should call `unscorable()` so the report is moved aside and the trial becomes `ERRORED-INFRA`.

comment_body:
`sed -i ''` is BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU sed (Linux, which is what this repo builds/runs on), `-i` doesn't take a separated argument — `''` gets parsed as the sed script (a no-op) and `'s/LogetoCreateTimeEntryRequest/LogetoTimeEntryRequest/g'` gets treated as a filename, which will fail with "No such file or directory" and silently skip the actual rename in every other file.

Suggest:
```bash
grep -rl --include='*.cs' LogetoCreateTimeEntryRequest backend | grep -v '/obj/' | \
  xargs sed -i 's/LogetoCreateTimeEntryRequest/LogetoTimeEntryRequest/g'
```
(no backup suffix needed, since this is git-tracked). Whoever executes this task will hit this immediately.

pr_title: docs: design and implementation plan for Logeto absence hours
comment_body:
Worth spelling out the failure mode here a bit more, since it's not just "narrower coverage" — it's a silent permanent gap. Because the window is `[max(StartDate, today - LookbackDays), today - 1]`, any timeless absence that ages past `LookbackDays` without being filled (e.g. the job is disabled, failing, or Logeto is unreachable for longer than `LookbackDays`) drops out of the window forever and is never revisited, with no counter or alert calling it out — it just quietly stops being candidate data. `SkippedNoHours`/`SkippedAmbiguous`/etc. only report on records currently inside the window, so there's no signal that older records were dropped without ever being processed.

Given `LookbackDays` defaults to 7 and the job ships disabled, this is a real risk during rollout (e.g. if enabling the job slips a couple weeks after merge). Not blocking, but consider either a generous default `LookbackDays` relative to expected rollout latency, or logging/counting how many days of window were skipped due to `StartDate`/`LookbackDays` clamping so the gap is visible rather than silent.

pr_title: chore: sync automerge/absorb skills with framework updates
comment_body:
**Potential data loss: `git reset --hard origin/<branch>` can silently discard local commits.**

Step 3 replaced `git pull origin <branch>` with `git fetch origin <branch>` + `git reset --hard origin/<branch>`. Unlike `git pull`, a hard reset doesn't attempt to reconcile local and remote history — it just throws away whatever is on the local branch that isn't on `origin/<branch>`, with no warning.

The step 1 safety check (`git status --porcelain`) only catches *uncommitted* working-tree changes. It doesn't protect against a scenario where the local branch has commits that were never pushed (e.g. a previous `/absorb` run's push failed partway, or someone committed locally on this exact branch outside the skill and re-runs `/absorb`) — those commits would be silently dropped by the reset with no error and no mention in the final summary.

Worth either: (a) checking `git rev-list origin/<branch>..<branch>` is empty before the reset and stopping/warning if not, or (b) keeping `git pull --ff-only` (or `merge`) here so a divergence surfaces as a merge/conflict instead of vanishing quietly.

pr_title: fix: discard stale background fetch pages on org/scope switch (GMC-43) [semantic pr title]
comment_body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Invalidate stale fetches before committing the context switch**

Because this generation bump runs in `useEffect`, it does not happen until after the render caused by `handleOrgContextChange`'s `setOwnerContext`/`setOwnerAffiliations` calls. If an old background page resolves in that gap, it still sees the previous generation as current and can append the old context's rows; this effect later clears only the cursors/loading flags, not `items`, so the stale rows can survive until the fresh first page lands and can still briefly re-open the corruption path this guard is meant to close. The generation needs to be invalidated from the synchronous context/scope-switch path, or the hook needs a synchronous reset API used before changing context.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

pr_title: Spike: TalkBack/gesture passthrough in :feature-carddeck
comment_body:
Approving. My understanding of what I'm approving: this is the apparatus for an answer, not the answer 
the spike has not been run, so we still don't know whether the card deck's gesture surface works with TalkBack, and we have no latency numbers.

    On that basis, three things I want held to:

        No feature-carddeck code gets built on the raw-touch assumption until the on-device run has happened.
        Running the spike is the next thing, not something that drifts.
        The Blocked on section in STATE.md and SPIKE.md stay until a verdict is actually recorded there.

    I've read the hypothesis and I'm not in a position to challenge it. If anyone is, do it before we act on it.
